_about: Objective software-engineering, testing and DevOps items.

mcq.q: A quick run after each build that checks the most critical paths still work is called:
mcq.answer: Smoke testing

mcq.q: Re-running tests to make sure new changes have not broken existing features is:
mcq.answer: Regression testing

mcq.q: Dividing inputs into valid and invalid classes and testing the edges of each is known as:
options: Equivalence partitioning with boundary value analysis
mcq.answer: Equivalence partitioning with boundary value analysis

mcq.q: A field accepts ages from 18 to 60 inclusive. Which values are the classic boundary tests?
Which practice writes a failing test before writing the production code?
mcq.answer: Test-driven development

mcq.q: A test double that returns canned answers without verifying how it was called is a:
mcq.answer: Stub

mcq.q: What does 100% line coverage guarantee?
options: Every line ran at least once — not that the behaviour is correct
mcq.answer: Every line ran at least once — not that the behaviour is correct

mcq.q: In Scrum, who owns and prioritises the product backlog?
mcq.answer: The Product Owner

mcq.q: What are Kanban's work-in-progress (WIP) limits meant to do?
mcq.answer: Reduce multitasking and expose bottlenecks

mcq.q: A library at version 2.3.1 adds a backward-compatible feature. What should the next version be?
A public API at version 1.9.4 introduces a breaking change. What should the next version be?
How does continuous delivery differ from continuous deployment?
options: Delivery keeps every change releasable but releases manually; deployment releases every passing change automatically
mcq.answer: Delivery keeps every change releasable but releases manually; deployment releases every passing change automatically

mcq.q: Which Git command safely undoes a pushed commit on a shared branch by creating a new commit?
mcq.answer: git revert

mcq.q: Trunk-based development relies on:
options: Small, frequent merges to main, often behind feature flags
mcq.answer: Small, frequent merges to main, often behind feature flags

mcq.q: What is the relationship between a Docker image and a container?
options: An image is a read-only template; a container is a running instance of it
An image is a running process
mcq.answer: An image is a read-only template; a container is a running instance of it

mcq.q: Which Dockerfile technique most reduces the final image size?
options: Multi-stage builds that copy only the build output into a slim base image
Installing development tools in the final stage
mcq.answer: Multi-stage builds that copy only the build output into a slim base image

mcq.q: What is the main job of a Kubernetes Deployment?
options: Keeping a desired number of pod replicas running and rolling out updates
mcq.answer: Keeping a desired number of pod replicas running and rolling out updates

mcq.q: What is a canary deployment?
options: Releasing to a small subset of users first and expanding if metrics stay healthy
Deploying to every server at once
mcq.answer: Releasing to a small subset of users first and expanding if metrics stay healthy

mcq.q: What does a blue-green deployment make easy?
options: Near-instant rollback by switching traffic back to the previous environment
Running two versions of the database schema forever
mcq.answer: Near-instant rollback by switching traffic back to the previous environment

mcq.q: Which of these is an infrastructure-as-code tool?
mcq.answer: Terraform

mcq.q: The four golden signals of monitoring are latency, traffic, errors and:
mcq.answer: Saturation

mcq.q: What does MTTR measure?
options: Mean time to recover from a failure
Mean time to release a feature
mcq.answer: Mean time to recover from a failure

mcq.q: A system has a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of 15 minutes. What does that mean?
options: At most 15 minutes of data may be lost in a disaster
The system must be restored within 15 minutes
mcq.answer: At most 15 minutes of data may be lost in a disaster

mcq.q: Which test checks that a system meets its targets under the expected peak load?
mcq.answer: Load testing

mcq.q: What is a flaky test?
options: A test that passes and fails intermittently without any code change
mcq.answer: A test that passes and fails intermittently without any code change

mcq.q: What does 'shift-left' testing mean?
options: Testing earlier in the development life cycle
mcq.answer: Testing earlier in the development life cycle

mcq.q: What should a blameless post-mortem focus on?
options: Systemic causes and preventive fixes rather than individual blame
mcq.answer: Systemic causes and preventive fixes rather than individual blame

mcq.q: Why is rebasing a shared, public branch risky?
options: It rewrites history that other developers have based work on
mcq.answer: It rewrites history that other developers have based work on

mcq.q: Which of these is a non-functional requirement?
options: Pages must load within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile
Customers can add items to a cart
mcq.answer: Pages must load within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile

mcq.q: What do feature flags allow teams to do?
options: Deploy code with a feature switched off and enable it independently of deployments
mcq.answer: Deploy code with a feature switched off and enable it independently of deployments
